speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see this newborn has increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin, suggesting jaundice. To determine the cause and severity, I need to ask a few questions and order some tests. First, how many days old is the baby, and when did you first notice the yellowing?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (likely due to insufficient intake/dehydration).

The history of increasing jaundice in a 2-week-old exclusively breastfed infant with no mention of dark urine or pale stools suggests a differential between physiological jaundice, breastfeeding jaundice (early), or breastfeeding jaundice (late). Given the age (2 weeks) and worsening symptoms, I need to rule out biliary atresia or other obstructive causes. REQUEST TEST: Total Serum Bilirubin, Direct (Conjugated) Bilirubin. REQUEST TEST: Urine Bilirubin and Urobilinogen. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound.
